key_insight: The paper reformulates FEM PDE solving in an augmented entanglement-basis space and uses tensor networks, so DMRG can optimize the solution with polynomial scaling in the number of finite elements when bond dimension is bounded.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable surrogate-style FEM solver for large solid-mechanics and PDE problems, especially where conventional high-dimensional assembly would be expensive.
method: Lift nonlinear FEM equations into an augmented coefficient space
Express governing PDEs, boundary/initial, and inter-element constraints as one quadratic residual minimization
Use MPS + DMRG sweeps to optimize element-by-element without explicitly building the full augmented space
evidence_signal: The abstract reports convergence on diffusion equations under both mesh refinement and polynomial refinement, indicating the approach is numerically consistent.
watch_item: Performance and accuracy depend on maintaining a bounded bond dimension; entanglement growth may reduce compression efficiency and increase cost.
paper_title: A Polynomial-Scaling PDE Solver with Entanglement-Basis Tensor Networks
